title: arXiv Biology and Biomedicine — Daily Report, 2026-10-23
global_caveat: ArXiv has no official trending chart. This relevance-ranked inference draws on a single announcement batch and incomplete arXiv biomedical coverage; many clinical and experimental preprints appear on bioRxiv or medRxiv instead.
arxiv_query: cat:q-bio.BM OR cat:q-bio.GN OR cat:q-bio.MN OR cat:q-bio.SC OR cat:q-bio.CB OR cat:q-bio.TO OR cat:q-bio.QM OR cat:cs.BI OR cat:physics.med-ph

sections.title: Headline
sections.content: This prior announcement batch yielded 12 notable papers from an 18-paper candidate pool. The strongest pattern is computational design and evaluation of RNA/protein systems, alongside early translational methods in imaging and radiochemistry. The agenda is mRNA and RNA–protein design, privacy-aware single-cell synthesis, molecular modeling, and biomedical measurement. This is a relevance-ranked inference, not an official arXiv trending chart: arXiv has no official popularity ranking, and its biology/biomedicine corpus is incomplete—many clinical and experimental preprints appear on bioRxiv or medRxiv instead.

sections.title: ProMORNA: An End-to-End Generative Framework for Full-Length mRNA Design
sections.abstract: ProMORNA generates full-length mRNA from a target protein sequence and reports improved in-silico stability/translation trade-offs plus higher reporter activity in three independent Fluc2P experiments.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors propose a zero-shot, end-to-end generator trained on more than six million protein–mRNA pairs, with supervised and multi-objective reinforcement-learning post-training.
sections.unique_caveat: Wet-lab testing covered seven selected candidates for one reporter protein. Candidate 2's 1.29× comparison with the reported best GEMORNA candidate did not remain significant after correction; reporter activity is not a direct measurement of mRNA stability or translation efficiency.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A substantive v2 revision appeared in this batch; authors report three independent in-vitro Fluc2P experiments and a Holm-adjusted 3.33× activity-AUC ratio versus the conventional benchmark. Relevance and reported evidence, not popularity, drive selection.

sections.title: RiboBridge: protein-conditioned de novo RNA binder structure design
sections.abstract: RiboBridge separates RNA-conformation generation from protein-relative assembly and predicts RNA–protein complex structures without a predefined binding site.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors use a pretrained RNA structural latent space, predicted protein-surface interface hypotheses and cross-frame interaction geometry to assemble candidate complexes.
sections.unique_caveat: The benchmark measures predicted structure recovery, not measured binding or biological activity; native interface information is used post hoc to select among already generated candidates, and interface prioritization and sequence realization remain unresolved.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Evaluated against existing methods on a temporally split, sequence-filtered and redundancy-controlled set of 124 protein–RNA complexes; authors report 20/124 targets reaching DockQ ≥ 0.23. Cross-listed in machine learning and biomolecules.

sections.title: Benchmarking Recent Single-Cell Synthetic Data Generation Methods on the OneK1K Dataset
sections.abstract: The authors compare scGFT, scLDM and Cell2Sentence for single-cell RNA-seq fidelity, biological-structure preservation and membership-inference risk on donor-split OneK1K data.
sections.claimed_contribution: The benchmark shows that post-processing and non-HVG handling materially change the privacy–utility balance; scGFT and scLDM retain more biological structure than an independent-Poisson baseline in reported tests.
sections.unique_caveat: Generative modeling was restricted to highly variable genes and evaluated on one dataset; privacy and biological-fidelity metrics can disagree, and metric choice and gene filtering affect conclusions.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Uses OneK1K (about 1.2 million PBMCs from 982 donors) and three evaluation axes; authors report non-HVG copying creates leakage while Poisson reconstruction reduces it. Presented at the CAMDA 2026 ELSA Health Privacy Challenge.

sections.title: Escaping the Phylogenetic Trap: Persistent Homology Enables Cross-Species Ion Channel Classification via Multimodal Graph Neural Networks
sections.abstract: A multimodal graph model uses persistent-homology features to classify venom ion-channel targets under leave-one-taxon-out evaluation.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors argue that topology-aware structural features help mitigate taxonomic leakage in cross-species ion-channel classification.
sections.unique_caveat: This is computational classification over predicted structures, not experimental toxin–channel binding or functional validation; performance is specific to the reported benchmark and split.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Benchmark includes 1,373 ColabFold-predicted venom compounds across five taxa; under taxon-held-out testing PH-GNN reaches 63.4%, versus 54–55% for next geometric priors.

sections.title: Behavioral Mapping of Hierarchical Dynamical Models Accelerates Bayesian Parameter Inference
sections.abstract: A behavioral-compatibility filter uses a simpler model's posterior to reduce costly Bayesian inference for a more detailed model, demonstrated on cell-free gene-expression models.
sections.claimed_contribution: The method learns a Gaussian-process level set of detailed-model parameters behaviorally supported by a reduced-model posterior, then filters proposals while retaining parameters that fit within a stated tolerance.
sections.unique_caveat: Evidence is from a hierarchy of cell-free gene-expression models; transfer to other model families or experimental regimes is not established, and speedup follows initial setup costs.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Authors report MCMC speedups of 8.02% for a phenomenological and 15.21% for a mechanistic gene-expression model after setup; cross-listed in quantitative biology, statistics and systems/control.

sections.title: Supercoiling Drives DNA-Protein Co-Condensation
sections.abstract: A coupled DNA-elasticity/protein-field model predicts that DNA supercoiling can facilitate protein wetting and co-condensation.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors propose DNA topology as a control parameter for biomolecular co-condensation and genome organization.
sections.unique_caveat: The result is model-based; it does not demonstrate the proposed pathway in cells or establish its quantitative importance in vivo.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Cross-listed across biological physics, soft matter and biomolecules; reports a model linking twist-to-writhe conversion, protein wetting and supercoiling-dependent nucleation.

sections.title: Direct Production of Ultra-High Radioisotopic Pure ⁶⁴Cu from Natural Zinc Metal via D-D Fusion Narrowband Fast Neutron Source Irradiation
sections.abstract: The authors report producing ⁶⁴Cu from natural zinc using a D-D fusion neutron source and measuring the irradiated sample by time-resolved gamma spectroscopy.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors present a potential alternative production route for copper-64, motivated by the cost of enriched nickel targets.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a production experiment, not a radiopharmaceutical formulation, animal study or clinical evaluation; reproducibility, scale-up and application-specific suitability remain unestablished.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: One-hour irradiation of high-purity natural zinc and 72-hour spectroscopy; authors report purity estimates of 99.62% and 99.97% after minimum-detection-activity correction.

sections.title: AI Enhanced Cerenkov Luminescence Microscopy
sections.abstract: A Monte-Carlo-guided CARE network restores simulated Cerenkov microscopy images and is applied to images from 27 radiotracer-exposed U87 tumor spheroids.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors propose physics-guided image restoration to mitigate noise and positron-induced blur in 3D Cerenkov luminescence microscopy.
sections.unique_caveat: Quantitative ground truth is simulated; spheroid image comparisons are not independent ground-truth recovery or in-vivo/clinical validation, and results depend on simulator fidelity.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Trained on 15,360 simulated image pairs from 80 geometries; synthetic validation MSE is 0.0051 versus 0.0492 for Noise2Void; applied to 27 experimental U87 spheroid images.

sections.title: Advancing oxygen-enhanced MRI acquisition and modelling through dynamic ΔR₁ and ΔR₂* sensing
sections.abstract: SR-Fat DESPOT combines fat–water-separated MRI acquisition with dynamic relaxation-rate modeling and is tested in a numerical phantom and small in-vivo studies.
sections.claimed_contribution: The proposed method aims to quantify fat- and water-specific baseline and gas-challenge-induced relaxation changes with fewer acquisitions.
sections.unique_caveat: In-vivo evidence is a six-person pilot plus a single-participant repeatability test; it does not establish diagnostic performance, generalizability or clinical utility.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Authors report phantom nMedAE below 3% at SNR >30, a one-participant test–retest study and a six-participant pilot under 100% oxygen, with statistically significant spleen and kidney changes.

sections.title: Geometry-Dependent Properties of Physically Crosslinked PPy-PVA Hydrogels Enable Tunable Iontophoretic Drug Delivery
sections.abstract: Five BSA-loaded PPy-PVA hydrogel geometries are compared for iontophoretic transport using Franz diffusion cells with artificial membranes.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors argue geometry can tune hydrogel microstructure, local fields and transport without changing current density for each design.
sections.unique_caveat: The reported payload is BSA and transport testing used artificial membranes; this does not establish delivery of a therapeutic through intact skin or in-vivo efficacy.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The abstract reports five geometries, permeability (3.80 ± 1.93) × 10⁻⁵, and a DOI registered to an IEEE Transactions on Biomedical Engineering article; checked against Crossref.

sections.title: Shorter but not more catalytic: an active-site-resolved model of how tau reshapes amyloid-β secondary nucleation
sections.abstract: A coupled tau–amyloid-β model tracks fibril mass, number and active secondary-nucleation sites to test when shorter fibrils change catalytic activity.
sections.claimed_contribution: The author identifies active-site density, exposure and monomer clearance/elongation balance as conditions governing modeled secondary-nucleation response.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a mechanistic model, not a new biochemical measurement; predictions need comparison with matched-mass fibril assays and measured active-site accessibility.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Model explores 800 Latin-hypercube samples and mean fibril lengths from 0.3 to 30 μm; predicts shortening alone does not necessarily increase catalytic activity.

sections.title: Global Convergence of Detailed Balanced Mass Action Systems
sections.abstract: The authors give a Lean 4-formalized proof that positive trajectories in finite detailed-balanced mass-action systems converge to a unique positive equilibrium in each positive compatibility class.
sections.claimed_contribution: The paper supplies a self-contained proof of uniqueness and global convergence for the stated class of detailed-balanced reaction networks.
sections.unique_caveat: The theorem is limited to finite, detailed-balanced deterministic systems with positive rate constants; it is not evidence about stochastic, noisy, non-detailed-balanced or experimentally measured networks.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Cross-listed in logic, dynamical systems and molecular networks; authors report complete formalization checked by the Lean kernel and provide a public Lean development.

sections.title: Trending Research Themes
sections.content: Protein/RNA design and sequence-to-function modeling: ProMORNA, RiboBridge and the ion-channel classifier use generative or structure-aware learning around biological sequences and structures. Mechanistic models spanning molecular organization and kinetics: supercoiling–co-condensation, tau/amyloid secondary nucleation and detailed-balanced mass-action convergence formalize molecular behavior with models or proofs. Biomedical methods paired with physical or experimental data: copper-64 production, Cerenkov microscopy, oxygen-enhanced MRI and hydrogel transport connect methods to measurements at different stages. Privacy-aware synthetic omics is represented by one OneK1K paper, not a recurring signal.

sections.title: Open Problems and Research Directions
sections.content: Expand mRNA and RNA-binder validation across targets and sequence lengths, with separate measurements of expression, stability, binding and function. Replicate the OneK1K privacy–utility study on independent cohorts, tissues and platforms, including full-transcriptome and donor-level privacy analyses. Test supercoiling and tau/amyloid model predictions with matched-condition experiments and direct site measurements. Extend radiochemistry, Cerenkov imaging, oxygen-MRI and hydrogel results through replication, independent phantoms/cohorts and biological-barrier validation; these are proposals, not results or clinical advice.

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.content: The batch is strongest in computational molecular design and evaluation, with a smaller set of measurement-oriented biomedical studies. ProMORNA is the clearest experimental bridge but remains a single-reporter study; RiboBridge and related modeling results are benchmark evidence, not confirmed molecular function. Imaging and delivery studies remain early-stage.
